title: Gingerbread Cookies
summary: Spiced treacle cookies, firm enough to cut into clean shapes and decorate once cooled.
equipment: 2 large metal baking trays lined with baking paper

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Melt butter, sugar and spices
steps.text: Melt the butter, sugar, treacle, spices and salt together in a saucepan over low heat, stirring until smooth, without letting it boil. Melting rather than creaming lets the treacle and spices disperse evenly through the fat before the dough comes together.

steps.title: Cool and add egg
steps.text: Pour the mixture into a bowl and leave to cool for 10 minutes until lukewarm, then beat in the egg. Cooling first stops the warm mixture from scrambling the egg as it goes in.

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Stir in the flour and bicarbonate of soda to form a soft, sticky dough, without adding extra flour even though it feels tacky. Extra flour at this stage dries the dough out and makes the baked cookies tough rather than tender.

steps.title: Chill the dough
steps.text: Pat the dough into 2 discs, wrap, and chill for at least 1 hour until firm enough to roll.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Turn the oven on to 175°C (155°C fan) at least 20 minutes before the first tray goes in.

steps.title: Roll and cut
steps.text: Roll each disc between sheets of baking paper to 5mm thick, cut out shapes, and re-roll the scraps once. Space the cut-outs 3cm apart on the lined metal trays.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake one tray at a time for 9-11 minutes, until the edges are firm and the tops look dry; thinner or smaller shapes need less time. The dough is already dark from the treacle, so judge doneness by firmness and dryness rather than colour.

steps.title: Cool on a rack
steps.text: Leave them on the tray for 5 minutes to firm up, then lift onto a wire rack until completely cold.

steps.title: Ice and decorate
steps.text: Mix the icing sugar with the lemon juice to a thick, pipeable paste, then decorate the cookies once they're completely cool. Leave to set for 1 hour before stacking or storing.

tips: Let the melted butter and treacle mixture cool to lukewarm before adding the egg, or the heat will scramble it and leave lumps in the dough.
Resist adding extra flour even though the dough feels sticky — it firms up considerably after chilling, and extra flour makes the baked cookies tough.
Watch for dry, firm tops rather than colour change when judging doneness — the dough is already dark from the treacle, so colour isn't a reliable cue.
Keep smaller or thinner cut-outs on their own tray, since they'll be ready before larger shapes and can scorch if left in alongside them.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep undecorated cookies in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 1 week, or freeze for up to 3 months. Iced cookies keep at room temperature for up to 5 days once the icing has set.
